chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Battle of Badr took place in the month of Ramadan, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not perform I'tikaf. When it was the following year, he performed I'tikaf for twenty nights: ten for his current year and ten as compensation for what was missed.
ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad perform I'tikaf during the Battle of Badr?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the flexibility of the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practice of I'tikaf, demonstrating that it was a recommended act (mustahabb) rather than an obligatory one, as he compensated for the missed nights only after the fact. The specific mention of the Battle of Badr provides historical context for the initial omission, while the subsequent twenty-night observance establishes a precedent for the duration of seclusion that later scholars, including the Shia Imams, often cited in their juristic discussions on the merits of the last ten days of Ramadan.
